newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks seen falling amid selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks seen falling amid selling pressure.

text.p: Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) may fall further amid selling pressure when the market reopens on Saturday, brokers said.
"Investors may remain somewhat nervous following a court order for the arrest of alleged market manipulators and may stay on the sidelines," said broker M.A. Hossain.
But he said the market may regain confidence within a couple of days. "There is no panic in the market. But investors may like to watch the market at the moment," he added.
Four of 36 dealers and company owners facing arrest for alleged manipulation of share prices in the stock market have already surrendered to the High Court and obtained bail.
A report into the affair has alleged the dealers and company owners had been involved in "fraudulent activities" causing volatile movements in share prices and losses to investors.
The DSE all-share price index closed 87.46 points or 7.13 percent down at 1,138.46 on Thursday. Friday is the Moslem weekend in Bangladesh.
